transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Welcome in—what brings you here to see me today?

What finally made me come in is, when my car gets onto one of those long bridges toward Miami, my chest tightens and my hands clamp down on the wheel. I suddenly feel like I have to get off right away, even though there’s nowhere to go.
Do these episodes of chest tightness and needing to escape only happen on bridges or similar situations, or have you ever had a sudden episode like this out of the blue, with no clear trigger?
It happens when I’m on those long bridges. The moment I get on one, my chest tightens, I grip the wheel, and I feel like I have to get off right away, even though I can’t.
Besides bridges, do you have similar fear or the urge to escape in other situations, like being in crowded places, open spaces, or far from home?
I haven’t really noticed it in other situations. It’s mainly the long bridges that set it off.
How long have you been experiencing this fear and urge to escape when crossing long bridges?
About 11 months now. It started around the time my daughter’s heart condition meant we had to make regular trips to specialists in Miami.
Have you started avoiding those long bridges altogether, like taking longer alternate routes or having someone else drive you across?

Yes. I’ve started turning down gallery openings, birdwatching trips, even some visits with my daughter unless someone else can drive me over the bridges. It’s embarrassing—I’ve always been the one who planned things and handled them myself.

Avoidance behavior and functional impairment (>6 months) further support this diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a marked, persistent fear specifically triggered by crossing long bridges, with immediate anxiety symptoms (chest tightness, gripping the wheel, urge to flee) that occur consistently in this specific situation. There is no evidence of unexpected panic attacks unrelated to the trigger, and fear does not generalize to other agoraphobic situations (crowds, open spaces, being away from home), ruling out panic disorder and agoraphobia. The fear has led to active avoidance behavior (declining trips, relying on others to drive) causing functional impairment, and has persisted for approximately 11 months, exceeding the duration threshold for phobic disorders. This presentation is consistent with a specific (situational) phobia.
